page: Microsoft Azure DC16eds_v6 is an Intel-powered virtual machine designed for general-purpose workloads that demand balanced memory allocation and fast local transient storage. Virtualized through Microsoft Hyper-V, the system provides 16 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs alongside 64.0 GB of system RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 processor-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The instance operates without discrete GPU accelerators, focusing entirely on general CPU compute capacity and direct input/output throughput.

A primary hardware differentiator of the DC16eds_v6 instance is the inclusion of 945 GB of integrated direct-attached NVMe SSD storage. This local volume provides low latency and high data transfer rates for temporary scratchpad data, intermediate caching, and high-frequency read and write operations. The instance does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring administrators to configure network routing and access via virtual network interfaces.

From a cost-efficiency and architecture perspective, the bundled NVMe storage minimizes the need to provision expensive, high-throughput network block storage for temporary data processing. However, a structural tradeoff is the ephemeral nature of direct-attached instance storage, necessitating externalized data persistence strategies for stateful services.

The DC16eds_v6 configuration is suited for workloads requiring a balanced distribution of processing cores, system memory, and rapid local scratch capacity. Representative use cases include transactional database engines, distributed caching nodes, intermediate data transformation pipelines, continuous integration build runners, and enterprise web application tiers.
description: Microsoft Azure DC16eds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization and powered by an x86_64 Intel processor. The instance provides 16 dedicated vCPUs matched with 64.0 GB of system memory, establishing a standard 4.0 GB per core resource profile. Local high-speed storage is integrated directly via a 945 GB NVMe solid-state drive, enabling rapid temporary read and write capabilities without relying entirely on remote network storage volumes. The instance includes no discrete graphics processing units and allocates zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring standard cloud networking interfaces for external communication. From an infrastructure perspective, bundling dense NVMe scratch capacity alongside a balanced memory-to-core allocation provides operational efficiency for intermediate caching and data manipulation. The configuration is particularly suited for production relational databases, enterprise software tiers, search indices, and continuous integration pipelines that benefit from fast local storage.
